Finally, the review does not focus on the concept of boundary (or micro-transitions), but more
generally on the work-life interface of academics. There is a lack of reasoned articulation of the
concept of boundary based on the readings included in the review (also because several of the
included studies do not use the concept of boundary - an aspect that I think needs to be argued
effectively).

Regarding the concept of boundaries, we recognize that we did not exclusively consider
studies that are specifically dedicated to this topic as we included research on work-life
balance and conflict. We did this because these areas also address boundary issues.
We now highlight that much of the existing research tends to focus on concepts rather than
seeking to develop an experiential understanding, which we also problematize in the
revised version.
